newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian race row MP wants tariffs back.
newsitem.headline: Australian race row MP wants tariffs back.

text.p: Australian race row politician Pauline Hanson, who hopes to hold the balance of power in parliament after the next election, called on Wednesday for tariff barriers to be rebuilt to protect Australian industry.
"I want to see the revitalisation of Australian industry and manufacturing," Hanson told a news conference in Adelaide ahead of the launch of her One Nation party in the city.
"If that means putting on tariff protection, well then we put on tariff protection," she said, adding that levels would be decided on a case-by-case basis.
"Other countries are laughing at us as we move our manufacturing offshore and create employment in their countries instead of our own," she said.

The populist mother-of-four from conservative Queensland state, elected to the national parliament as an independent last year, has been steadily wooing voters since she lifted her ambitions and launched her own party in April.
Apart from higher tariffs, Hanson has also called for an immediate end to immigration.
Leading opinion polls rank One Nation as the third most popular political group, after the ruling Liberal/National coalition and the opposition Labor Party.
With candidates to be selected for her party over the coming months, Hanson said One Nation would be contesting every seat in Australia at the next election, due in 1999.
"I am wanting to have enough people in those seats to actually be an influence on government policy," she said.
